newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spain's BCH to control biggest Chilean bank.
newsitem.headline: Spain's BCH to control biggest Chilean bank.

text.p: Chile's central bank on Thursday approved a merger that would make Banco de Santiago, which is 51 percent controlled by Spain's BCH, the largest in the country, Banco Central Hispano-BCH said.
The new bank, formed from the merger of Banco de Santiago and Banco O'Higgins, has $11.33 billion in assets, profits to June 1996 of $97 million and a 21-percent market share.
The new Banco de Santiago will quote on the New York Stock Exchange with a market value of $2.32 million.
It will specialise in univeral banking emphasising individual, private banking and consumer credit, which will be reinforced through BCH's proven credit system "Creditscoring", the bank said.

The new bank will put a priority on pension fund management, using AFP Qualitas, a Chilean specialist owned by BCH. The bank also aims to enter in the insurance market and is in the market for a life insurance company.
The merger reinforces BCH's presence in Chile, which it says has the best potential in Latin America with "a solid, established political, social and economic system".
